sections.heading: The Cell as the Unit of Life

note_sections.heading: The Cell as the Unit of Life
note_sections.body_md:
### What a cell is

A **cell** is the smallest arrangement of matter that carries out every activity associated with being alive [chunk:b10c0000]. Some organisms complete their entire life cycle as a single cell, while plants and animals are assemblies of trillions of specialised cells [chunk:b10c0000].

### Cell theory

The **cell theory** holds that all living organisms are composed of one or more cells [chunk:b10c0000]. It further holds that the cell is the basic unit of structure and organisation in organisms [chunk:b10c0000]. Its third statement, that cells arise only from pre-existing cells by division, was the last to be established [chunk:b10c0000].

### Why cells stay small

As a sphere grows, volume increases with the cube of the radius while surface area increases only with the square [chunk:b10c0000]. A cell that doubles in radius therefore has eight times as much interior to supply but only four times as much membrane to supply it through [chunk:b10c0000]. This surface-area-to-volume constraint is why most cells measure between one and one hundred micrometres across [chunk:b10c0000].

note_sections.heading: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic Cells
note_sections.body_md:
### The dividing line

**Prokaryotic** cells keep their DNA in an irregular cytoplasmic region called the nucleoid, with no membrane separating it from the rest of the interior [chunk:b10c0000]. **Eukaryotic** cells enclose their DNA inside a true nucleus bounded by a double membrane [chunk:b10c0000].

### Compartmentalisation

Eukaryotic cells are filled with membrane-bound organelles, each maintaining chemical conditions different from the surrounding cytoplasm [chunk:b10c0001]. Compartmentalisation lets a eukaryotic cell run incompatible reactions simultaneously in different places [chunk:b10c0001]. Prokaryotic cells manage without this internal partitioning, which is one reason they are typically ten times smaller in diameter [chunk:b10c0001].

### What both share

Both categories are bounded by a plasma membrane, contain cytoplasm, carry hereditary information in DNA, and build proteins on ribosomes [chunk:b10c0001]. Ribosomes in prokaryotes are somewhat smaller than those in eukaryotes [chunk:b10c0001].

note_sections.heading: The Plasma Membrane
note_sections.body_md:
### Structure

The plasma membrane is a **phospholipid bilayer** studded with proteins [chunk:b10c0001]. Each phospholipid has a phosphate head attracted to water and two fatty acid tails repelled by it, so in water the molecules arrange themselves spontaneously into a double sheet [chunk:b10c0001]. No energy input is required, because that arrangement is simply the lowest-energy configuration available [chunk:b10c0001].

### Selective permeability

The resulting sheet is **selectively permeable** [chunk:b10c0001]. Small non-polar molecules such as oxygen and carbon dioxide pass through the fatty interior unaided, while ions and large polar molecules must cross through protein channels and transporters [chunk:b10c0001]. **Passive transport** moves substances down a concentration gradient at no energy cost, whereas **active transport** consumes ATP to push them against their gradient [chunk:b10c0001]. The sodium-potassium pump exports three sodium ions for every two potassium ions it imports [chunk:b10c0001].

### Fluid mosaic model

Because the phospholipids are not bonded to one another they drift laterally, so the membrane behaves as a two-dimensional fluid with proteins floating in it [chunk:b10c0001]. This is why membranes can heal small punctures, fuse, and pinch off into vesicles [chunk:b10c0001].

note_sections.heading: The Endomembrane System
note_sections.body_md:
### Nucleus and ribosomes

The **nucleus** is the largest organelle in most animal cells and holds nearly all of the cell's DNA behind a double membrane called the nuclear envelope [chunk:b10c0002]. DNA is wound around histone proteins into chromatin, which condenses into visible chromosomes only when the cell prepares to divide [chunk:b10c0002]. **Ribosomes** are the sites of protein synthesis and, unlike the other structures here, are not bounded by a membrane [chunk:b10c0002].

### ER and Golgi

Rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with ribosomes and folds and chemically tags newly made proteins [chunk:b10c0002]. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesises lipids, stores calcium ions, and detoxifies drugs and metabolic byproducts [chunk:b10c0002]. The **Golgi apparatus** sorts, modifies, and packages proteins for delivery, taking material in on the face nearest the endoplasmic reticulum [chunk:b10c0002].

### Lysosomes

Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs of digestive enzymes held at an interior pH near five, well below the neutral cytoplasm around them [chunk:b10c0002]. Because those enzymes work poorly at cytoplasmic pH, a leaking lysosome does comparatively little damage [chunk:b10c0002].

note_sections.heading: Energy Organelles and the Cytoskeleton
note_sections.body_md:
### Mitochondria

**Mitochondria** carry out cellular respiration, the controlled oxidation of sugars that transfers energy into ATP [chunk:b10c0002]. Each has a smooth outer membrane and an inner membrane folded into cristae, and the folding matters because oxidative phosphorylation happens on that inner membrane [chunk:b10c0002].

### Chloroplasts

**Chloroplasts** occur in plants and algae and carry out photosynthesis, capturing light energy to build sugars from carbon dioxide and water [chunk:b10c0003]. They contain stacked discs called thylakoids where chlorophyll is concentrated, suspended in a fluid called the stroma [chunk:b10c0003]. Both mitochondria and chloroplasts hold their own circular DNA and ribosomes and divide independently, which is the evidence behind the **endosymbiotic theory** [chunk:b10c0003].

### Cytoskeleton and cell wall

The cytoskeleton is a network of protein filaments that gives the cell shape, anchors organelles, and provides tracks for motor proteins [chunk:b10c0003]. Microtubules are hollow tubes of tubulin that form the spindle separating chromosomes during division [chunk:b10c0003]. Plant cells add a rigid cell wall built mainly of cellulose, which resists the turgor pressure that holds a non-woody plant upright [chunk:b10c0003]. Animal cells have no wall and depend on the cytoskeleton for structural support.

> Not in your materials: the detailed steps of glycolysis and the Calvin cycle.

quiz.title: Cell Structure and the Organelles — Quiz

questions.topic: The Cell as the Unit of Life
questions.prompt: A spherical cell doubles its radius. By what factor does the interior volume it must supply increase relative to the membrane area available for exchange?
options: The volume doubles while the area stays fixed
The volume increases eightfold while the area increases fourfold
questions.answer: The volume increases eightfold while the area increases fourfold
questions.explanation: Volume scales with the cube of the radius and surface area with the square, so doubling the radius gives eight times the volume but only four times the area [chunk:b10c0000].

questions.prompt: Which feature is present in eukaryotic cells but absent from prokaryotic cells?
options: A nucleus bounded by a double membrane
questions.answer: A nucleus bounded by a double membrane
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes keep their DNA in a nucleoid with no surrounding membrane, while eukaryotes enclose it in a true nucleus; membranes, ribosomes and DNA are common to both [chunk:b10c0000].

questions.prompt: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer spontaneously in water?
options: Because ATP hydrolysis drives the assembly
Because it is the lowest-energy configuration for heads attracted to water and tails repelled by it
Because membrane proteins bond them together
Because the cell wall forces them into sheets
questions.answer: Because it is the lowest-energy configuration for heads attracted to water and tails repelled by it
questions.explanation: The arrangement requires no energy input; it is simply the lowest-energy configuration available to molecules with a water-attracted head and water-repelled tails [chunk:b10c0001].

questions.prompt: The inner mitochondrial membrane is folded into cristae. What is the functional consequence?
options: It multiplies the area available for oxidative phosphorylation
It anchors the cell to neighbouring cells
questions.answer: It multiplies the area available for oxidative phosphorylation
questions.explanation: Oxidative phosphorylation occurs on the inner membrane, so folding it into cristae multiplies the productive area [chunk:b10c0002].

questions.prompt: Ribosomes are enclosed by their own membrane, like the other organelles described in this chapter.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are complexes of RNA and protein and, unlike most structures in the chapter, are not bounded by a membrane [chunk:b10c0002].

questions.prompt: Compartmentalisation allows a eukaryotic cell to run chemically incompatible reactions at the same time.
questions.explanation: Membrane-bound compartments maintain conditions different from the cytoplasm, so incompatible reactions can proceed simultaneously in different places [chunk:b10c0001].

questions.prompt: Digestive enzymes are held inside membrane-bound sacs at an interior pH near five; these sacs are called ______.
questions.explanation: The chapter describes these acidic enzyme-filled sacs, which recycle worn-out organelles and engulfed bacteria [chunk:b10c0002].

questions.prompt: The rigid outer layer of a plant cell is built mainly from ______, and it resists the outward pressure of the water-filled central vacuole.
questions.explanation: The plant cell wall is built mainly of this polysaccharide and resists turgor pressure [chunk:b10c0003].

questions.prompt: State two pieces of evidence given for the endosymbiotic theory.
questions.answer: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own circular DNA and their own ribosomes, and they divide independently of the cell.
questions.explanation: Both organelles retain prokaryote-like genetic machinery and divide on their own schedule, which is what the theory predicts [chunk:b10c0003].

questions.prompt: For every two potassium ions the sodium-potassium pump imports, how many sodium ions does it export?
questions.explanation: The pump moves sodium out and potassium in against their gradients using ATP [chunk:b10c0001].
